title: MSP-MVS Multi-granularity Segmentation Prior Guided Multi-View Stereo

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper is titled/abstracted as "MSP-MVS" (multi-granularity segmentation prior, anchor equidistribution, iterative local search), yet the introduction states "we propose TSAR-MVS, a generalized post-processing MVS method that sequentially applies confidence-based outliers filtering, superpixel-based local refinement, and feature-based area generation". This is a different method entirely and directly contradicts the abstract, method sections and conclusion.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, "In summary, our contributions are as follows" (items 1–3)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The listed contributions (joint hypothesis filter with confidence estimator/disparity discontinuity, iterative correlation refinement with RANSAC+WMF, textureless-aware segmentation via Roberts edge + Hough line detection) do not correspond to any component of MSP-MVS described in the abstract, method, ablation or conclusion (multi-granularity segmentation prior, anchor equidistribution, iterative local search optimization). The contribution list belongs to a different paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction ("Experiments on extensive datasets...") vs. Experiments section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction claims experiments on "the ETH3D high-resolution dataset, Tanks & Temples dataset and Strecha dataset", but the experiments section states only "We evaluate our work on ETH3D benchmark ... and Tanks & Temples benchmark (TNT)". No Strecha results are reported anywhere.

predicted_errors.error_location: Related Work ("TAPA-MVS ..., PCF-MVS ... and TSAR-MVS (Yuan et al. 2024b) attempt to employ superpixel planarization")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: TSAR-MVS is cited as a competing prior work, while the introduction simultaneously claims "we propose TSAR-MVS" as this paper's contribution. The paper cannot both propose and cite TSAR-MVS as prior art; one of the two statements is incorrect.

"Both w/o. Her. and w/o. Agr. produce similar better results than w/o. CRF., yet are inferior to MSP-MVS, indicating that both multi-granularity SAM prior and aggregation are equally crucial than edge correction." The logic is inverted/incoherent: if ablating the multi-granularity prior and the aggregation degrades performance less than ablating edge correction, then those components are LESS crucial than edge correction, not "equally crucial". The same ablation style in the other two paragraphs uses the opposite (correct) reasoning, exposing the inconsistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Related Work, learning-based paragraph ("Cas-MVSNet (Yang et al. 2020)")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Yang et al. 2020, "Cost Volume Pyramid Based Depth Inference for Multi-View Stereo" is CVP-MVSNet, not Cas-MVSNet (Gu et al., CVPR 2020, "Cascade Cost Volume for High-Resolution Multi-View Stereo and Stereo Matching"). The reference is misattributed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, learning-based methods paragraph ("several methods like (Wang et al. 2021) attempt to employ lightweight gated recurrent units (GRU)")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: PatchmatchNet (Wang et al. 2021) does not use GRUs; it implements a learned PatchMatch with adaptive propagation and evaluation. The GRU-based probability encoding described belongs to IterMVS (Wang et al. 2022a). The claim misrepresents the cited work.

Semantic-SAM is the central tool of the proposed method ("we adopt the Semantic-SAM to extract multi-granularity depth edges") but is never cited; only SAM (Kirillov et al. 2023) appears in the reference list. A key external model is used without attribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method / Ablation (iterative local search optimization, aggregation, edge correction)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Components evaluated in the ablation (ILS with 'variance' and 'cost' terms, multi-granularity aggregation, CRF-based edge correction, anchor clustering) are never defined or described in the method text. The paper cannot be reproduced or verified; the ablation refers to steps absent from the described pipeline.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, learning-based methods paragraph ("(Yang et al. 2020; Luo et al. 2019) leverage a coarse-to-fine cascading architecture")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: P-MVSNet (Luo et al. 2019) is a patch-wise matching confidence aggregation network with a hybrid 3D U-Net, not a coarse-to-fine cascading/upsampling architecture; the attribution misrepresents the cited work.

"we propose adaptive equidistribution, which uniformly divides the homogeneous area of each unreliable pixel into eight sectors based on the number of its surrounding reliable pixels" is self-contradictory: a fixed division into eight sectors cannot simultaneously be determined by the varying number of surrounding reliable pixels. Also the component is named "anchor equidistribution" in the abstract, ablation and conclusion, but "adaptive equidistribution" here.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Conclusion vs. Experiments (TNT advanced results)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract/conclusion assert "state-of-the-art results on ETH3D and Tanks & Temples benchmarks", but the experiments report only second-best F1 on the TNT advanced set ("falling short by less than 0.3% in F1 score compared to EPNet"), so the blanket SOTA claim on Tanks & Temples is overstated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section, two consecutive paragraphs on Semantic-SAM
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paragraph beginning "Due to the absence of depth edge as constraints, APD-MVS erroneously skips depth edges..." is duplicated almost verbatim by the subsequent paragraph ("Since APD-MVS lacks depth edge guidance, its anchors typically skip depth edges..."), including identical sentences about Semantic-SAM's semantic awareness and granularity richness. This redundant duplication indicates an editing/integrity error in the manuscript.
